statement: When the canvas URL recorded in design-map.json returns not-found from the current account, `/refine-design` publishes a new canvas from the committed files under `docs/ui/<slug>/canvas/`, records the new URL, carries on, and does not end COMMAND STUCK
evidence: Headless fixture-session transcript of `/refine-design` on a design whose design-map.json canvas URL points at a non-existent artifact: shows the not-found read, an Artifact publish from `docs/ui/<slug>/canvas/`, the run continuing, and a final `COMMAND COMPLETE` banner (no `COMMAND STUCK`); plus the design-map.json after the run holding the new URL

statement: When the canvas URL recorded in design-map.json returns no-access from the current account, `/refine-design` publishes a new canvas from `docs/ui/<slug>/canvas/`, records the new URL, carries on, and does not end COMMAND STUCK
evidence: Same as FS-1, with the recorded canvas URL pointing at an artifact the fixture session's account cannot open: transcript showing the no-access read, the republish, and a `COMMAND COMPLETE` banner; design-map.json holding the new URL

statement: When the Design System page recorded in `design_system.url` returns not-found or no-access from the current account, `/design-system --sync` publishes a new Design System page from the committed files under `docs/ui/_design-system/<folder>/`, records the new URL, carries on, and does not end COMMAND STUCK
evidence: Headless fixture-session transcript of `/design-system --sync` with `design_system.url` set to an unreachable artifact: shows the not-found/no-access read, an Artifact publish from `docs/ui/_design-system/<folder>/`, and a `COMMAND COMPLETE` banner; the file holding `design_system.url` after the run showing the new URL

statement: After a canvas is republished, its design-map.json entry holds the new URL and keeps the replaced URL as `previous_url`
cites: #150 Expected ("record the new URL with the old one kept as previous_url (map entries …)")
evidence: design-map.json from the FS-1 or FS-2 run, showing the canvas entry's new URL and `previous_url` equal to the URL that failed to read

statement: After a canvas or Design System page is republished, its artifacts.json entry holds the new URL and keeps the replaced URL as `previous_url`
evidence: `.trd-state/<feature>/artifacts.json` (fetched from the records ref if not in the worktree) after the FS-1/FS-2 and FS-3 runs, showing the replaced entry's new `url` and `previous_url` equal to the old one

statement: When the Design System page is republished, the place that records `design_system.url` holds the new URL and keeps the replaced URL as `previous_url`
cites: #150 Expected ("record the new URL with the old one kept as previous_url")
evidence: The file holding `design_system.url` after the FS-3 run, showing the new URL and `previous_url` equal to the URL that failed to read

statement: The library that writes artifacts.json entries accepts a `previous_url` and keeps it in the entry it writes (today `previous_url` exists nowhere in lib/)
cites: #150 Lib; domain-derived: artifacts.json entries are written only through the project's artifact-record library helper, so the #150 Expected requirement that artifacts.json entries keep `previous_url` cannot be met unless that helper preserves the field
evidence: Output of the artifact-record library CLI (`record` then `get`/`read`) run locally against a scratch state folder, showing an entry recorded with a `previous_url` and read back with it intact

statement: When a canvas or the Design System page is replaced, the command's readout says so in its DECISIONS section
evidence: The final readout of the FS-1/FS-2 and FS-3 runs: the `DECISIONS` section contains a line stating the canvas (or system page) was republished because the recorded one could not be read, naming the new URL

statement: A republished canvas starts a fresh sync base: the sync base recorded after the republish belongs to the new canvas, not one carried over from the replaced URL
evidence: design-map.json (and any sync-base record the run writes) after the FS-1 run, showing the sync base reset to the newly published canvas rather than the old canvas's prior sync state

statement: A canvas or Design System page read that fails with any error other than not-found or no-access does not trigger a republish: no new artifact is published, the recorded URL is unchanged, and no `previous_url` is written
evidence: Headless fixture-session transcript of `/refine-design` (or `/design-system --sync`) where the canvas read fails with a different error, showing no publish call; design-map.json and artifacts.json after the run with the original URL and no `previous_url`

statement: `/audit-design` labels each below-floor contrast miss and each below-44px target-size miss as either drawn by this design or on a reused component unchanged through `x-import`
evidence: `/audit-design` report from a fixture design holding one hand-drawn element below the contrast floor and one library component reused unchanged through `x-import` that is also below floor: the two findings carry different labels ("drawn by this design" versus "reused component, unchanged")

statement: A below-floor contrast or target-size miss on an element drawn by this design is ranked high, including when a build-side caveat ruling is recorded for reused components
evidence: The FS-11 report, and a second `/audit-design` report after a ruling is recorded in brief.md `## Accessibility caveats`: in both, the hand-drawn miss is ranked high

statement: With an accept or fix-in-build ruling recorded in brief.md `## Accessibility caveats`, `/audit-design` shows a below-floor miss on a reused, unchanged component as a known build-side caveat instead of a high finding
evidence: `/audit-design` report on the FS-11 fixture after adding the reused component's ruling to brief.md `## Accessibility caveats`: the reused miss appears as a known build-side caveat and not as a high finding

statement: With an accept or fix-in-build ruling recorded in design.md section 4, `/audit-design` shows a below-floor miss on a reused, unchanged component as a known build-side caveat instead of a high finding
evidence: `/audit-design` report on the FS-11 fixture with the ruling recorded only in the fixture's design.md section 4 (brief.md carrying none): the reused miss appears as a known build-side caveat and not as a high finding

statement: With no ruling recorded in either brief.md or design.md section 4, a below-floor miss on a reused, unchanged component is not shown as a known build-side caveat
cites: #152 Caveats ("when such a ruling is recorded")
evidence: The FS-11 report (no ruling recorded anywhere): the reused miss is reported as a finding, with no build-side-caveat label
`git diff --stat` (or a before/after sha256) of the fixture's design.md across the FS-14 run, showing no change

statement: A disabled control (one carrying the `disabled` attribute or `aria-disabled`) is not reported for a contrast miss
evidence: `/audit-design` report on a fixture board holding a below-floor control marked `disabled` and another marked `aria-disabled`: neither has a contrast finding

statement: Text explaining why a control is disabled is still measured for contrast, and a disabled control below 44px is still reported for target size
cites: #152 Disabled ("text explaining why is still measured, target size not exempt")
evidence: The FS-17 report, with that fixture also holding below-floor explanatory text next to the disabled control and the disabled control sized below 44px: the text carries a contrast finding and the control carries a target-size finding

statement: `/refine-design` run with no feedback skips findings marked as recorded build-side caveats: it does not act on them, while other findings are still worked
evidence: Headless fixture-session transcript of `/refine-design` with no feedback, on a design whose audit holds one recorded build-side caveat and one ordinary finding: the readout shows the caveat skipped and the ordinary finding addressed, and the board carrying the caveated component is not redrawn for it
